title: Rapid triage playbook for admin & access requests (RBAC / SSO / SCIM / org policies)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a concise, actionable playbook and automated routing rules for inbound admin & access management requests from customers (RBAC templates, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning gaps, org policy exceptions). The goal is to reduce mean time to decision, ensure correct routing to Identity/Platform/Security, and produce deterministic prioritization signals for Product and Eng. This is non-bug intake: feature/permissions/configuration/entitlement requests that require product decisions, compliance input, or pre-approved patterns.
acceptance_criteria: A short (one-page) triage playbook exists and is discoverable by support/solutions/SEs
Automated intake form captures the rubric fields and sets a triage score without manual edits 80%+ of the time
Routing rules map 90% of incoming requests to the correct queue (Identity / Platform / Security) in the pilot week
Escalation matrix reduces time-to-first-response for high-impact access requests to under 4 hours
Playbook includes three example decision scenarios and owners for each path
Metrics dashboard tracks triage score distribution, routing accuracy, and SLA attainment
triage_rubric: Weighting model (0-100 score): Customer tier (30%), Security/regulatory risk (25%), Production impact (#users+latency) (20%), Repeat frequency (10%), Implementation complexity (10%), Time-sensitivity (5%)
Customer tier scoring: Enterprise (30), Mid-market (20), Startup/free (10)
Security/regulatory risk scoring examples: PII exposure or audit scope (25), potential data exfiltration vector (20), low-risk role change (5)
Implementation complexity: Self-service config (0-5), Console change + DB migration (6-15), Cross-team workflow + infra change (16-25)
Repeat frequency bonus: +10 if reported by 3+ tenants or 2+ accounts in 14 days
Thresholds: 70+ = P0/P1 review within 4 hours, 45-69 = P2 triage within 48 hours, <45 = backlog grooming cadence
routing_rules: If triage score >= 70 and security/regulatory risk >= 15 -> route to Security ops + Product
If request mentions SCIM provisioning gaps or failures -> route to Identity platform queue with SCIM tag
SSO/SAML onboarding with >100 seats -> route to Solutions Eng + Customer Engineering for assisted onboarding
RBAC template requests that fit an approved pattern -> auto-approve for self-serve and schedule doc update; else route to Platform for policy change
Org policy exception requests -> create incident ticket and add legal/compliance reviewer in notifications
escalation_matrix: P0 (score >= 90): immediate pager to on-call Platform + Product lead; SLAs: acknowledge in 1 hour, decision in 8 hours
P1 (70-89): notify Product triage channel; acknowledge in 4 hours, decision in 48 hours
P2 (45-69): queue for next Product grooming; initial reply within 3 business days
P3 (<45): document as product backlog candidate, auto-reply with expected review window of 2 cycles
intake_form_fields: Type: RBAC change | SSO/SAML onboarding | SCIM provisioning | Org policy exception | Other
Estimated number of affected users / orgs
Attachments: logs, SAML metadata, SCIM error traces, screenshots
Is this a repeat request? link other tickets
decisions: Use a single numeric triage score to drive routing and SLA assignment instead of separate binary flows
Expose triage score and rationale to customers for transparency on high-impact requests
Automate routing for SCIM/SSO keywords and require manual review for org policy exceptions
Pilot auto-approval for three low-risk RBAC templates to reduce manual work
open_questions: What is the visibility threshold where customer-facing triage reasons are shared versus internal notes?
Do we tie triage score directly to billing or SLA credits for enterprise customers?
Which exact metrics should the dashboard surface for executive reporting?
Who signs off on the initial set of auto-approved RBAC templates?
